answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works by requiring every agent to post a bond that is cheap once but costly across thousands of fake identities. An attacker plotting a voyage into the network cannot register a swarm for free: each instance locks collateral, and if one account is caught colluding, the whole cluster forfeits. Reputation pins to that stake like an atlas fixing coordinates, so fresh unproven agents earn no weight and cannot steer payouts. Casting millions of copies costs more than honest work, keeping the horizon of rewards unprofitable.
